question: A user has iterated on a code artifact through four rounds of edits and now decides the second version was actually the best one. How can the user return to that earlier version?
options: A) Start an entirely new conversation, since artifact versions cannot be recovered once a newer version has been created
B) Use the artifact's version selector to switch back to the second version, since each iteration is preserved and can be revisited
C) Ask Claude to recall the exact wording of the second version from memory, since earlier artifact versions are not stored anywhere
D) Manually retype the second version from the chat history, since artifacts only ever display the most recent iteration
correct_answers: B) Use the artifact's version selector to switch back to the second version, since each iteration is preserved and can be revisited
explanations: Incorrect. Version history persists within the same conversation, so starting a new conversation is not required to view an earlier version.
Correct. The artifact interface includes a version selector that lets users switch between prior iterations of the same artifact without losing any of them.
Incorrect. Prior versions are stored and browsable through the version selector, not something Claude needs to reconstruct from memory.
Incorrect. Artifacts retain their edit history, so manually retyping an earlier version is unnecessary.
